calendar_scope: All eight scheduled FOMC policy meetings in 2025; August notation vote excluded because it was not a regular meeting.
theme_selection: Tariff inflation selected after prior pilot; contiguous census reduces within-year date selection, not a blind evaluation. Manual selective claim excerpts, not exhaustive semantic annotation. Nonappearance of theme is not absence of belief.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Businesses expected to pass higher potential tariff-related input costs to buyers.
Inflation was expected to move toward target under appropriate monetary policy; trade and immigration policy could impede progress.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Size and persistence of tariff inflation were uncertain; intermediate inputs, supply-chain changes and expectations mattered.
Household savings depletion could constrain willingness to accept higher prices.
Contacts reported anticipated costs or willingness to raise consumer prices.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Business contacts or surveys indicated planned partial or full cost pass-through.
Tariffs on intermediate goods could prolong inflation.
Supply-chain disruption might prolong price pressures.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Pre-tariff stocks and intermediate inputs could delay final-goods price increases.
Weak tolerance for price increases or pursuit of market share could limit pass-through.
Expected a one-time price increase without a change in longer-run inflation expectations.
Noted possible longer-lasting inflation effects.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Tariff effects appeared in rising goods inflation as services inflation slowed.
Inventory buffers and gradual contract repricing could delay full effects.
Contacts reported supplier changes, reduced margins and efficiency efforts to limit price increases.
Expected a temporary price-level adjustment over a contained period.
Supply-chain disruption could prolong inflation.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Tariff inflation appeared weaker than expected earlier in the year.
Expected tariff effects to be realized by end-2026.
Continued productivity gains could reduce inflation pressure.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Expected further core goods price increases over coming quarters partly from tariff transmission.
Businesses reportedly waited for policy clarity before adjusting prices.
AI and automation productivity might preserve margins and limit consumer cost pass-through.

meetings.section: Participants' Views on Current Conditions and the Economic Outlook

claims.paraphrase: Attributed higher core inflation to tariffs through goods prices.
Expected tariff effects on goods inflation to diminish, timing and pass-through uncertain for some.
Contacts reported non-tariff input costs; some participants noted demand limits or productivity as potential offsets.

cross_strata.actor: Survey of nearly 6000 executives in US, UK, Germany and Australia
cross_strata.observation: More than 80% of firms reported no AI impact on employment or productivity over the preceding three years; firms anticipate gains in productivity and modest employment reductions over the next three years.
cross_strata.limit: Retrospective self-report, not measured aggregate productivity or a US-only survey. Expectations differ in horizon and population from SPF GDP/payroll forecasts. No quantitative subtraction.
cross_strata.research_use: Competing explanation for growth/jobs decoupling: realized productivity gains may lag adoption; test actual aggregate output per hour and sector mix independently.
